design_rationale:
WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. Joan Calloway asks only to pay her father's December Medicare coinsurance by card. Nothing for December is billed to the resident yet: the December block b6959ca7-0102-4c57-ac00-b5d846a9201c carries only the carrier's charge. The card rule states its wait in state form ("A card payment toward a coinsurance block is taken only after the records carry a resident coinsurance charge for the coverage's latest booked coinsurance block, whenever that block's covered days take a resident share above nothing under the split in effect on them."), so the agent must find the missing resident charge, price it with the charge policy and post it, then hand the card payment over. Pricing is the hard part: plan K -> plan L from 2025-12-16 (same carrier), the earlier share read from the November charge, a held hospital leave (bed-hold product), a one-night inpatient admission whose hold was declined (hospital-day reversal), two uncertified days after a late recertification, and the 2025 rate on a block posted in 2026.

SCOPE. Task 0 claims medicare_ext_resident_block_share (post_coinsurance_charge_97c12690, agent) and medicare_ext_card_payment_share (pay_coinsurance_by_card_ebeca5a6, user). Task 1 claims the rate-year correction, the reduction for reversed covered days and the bank-draft payment. Disjoint; all five extended policies covered.

POLICY / FACTOR CARD (round 2 structure, both computations). Amount = rate x (E x s_e + (D - E) x s_l) / 100 rounded half up once; s_l = resident share of the tier on file (plan L, 25 percent; non-factor base read); E = calendar days before the supplemental effective date (non-factor base split, 15) less the day kinds below. overwrite: medicare_evt_coinsurance split sentence, self-naming scope (record test: one December days_21_100 entry, one block before, one held leave with no held day taken back, at most one reversal per reason and no booking error, no hospital/leave reversal on a held night, the uncertified reversal counting its span less the other kinds inside it, block before billed at exactly 50 percent); out of scope the base split is restated and the policy prices nothing. Factors (draw [5, 5]):
- f_year_rate (P): 2025 -> 209.50; baseline 217.00 -> 1953.00.
- f_carried_split (P): November charge df1b6673-31ce-44b4-9b9b-78e99803d9c8 bills 628.50 = 50.0 percent of its own 6 x 209.50 (gross, own rate) -> 50; baseline 100 -> 2933.00.
- f_held_nights (M, multi-source, cross-difficulty bedhold): leave 1040aa5a-21a4-406e-bc5c-abf86251d9df 2025-12-06..07 inside the block, before 2025-12-16 -> 2; baseline 0 -> 1990.25.
- f_hospital_reversal (M, multi-source): reversal 4c95d7f4-e62d-4590-89b1-88c05564fd5c 2025-12-10 (hold declined, booked then reversed) -> 1; baseline 0 -> 1937.88.
- f_uncertified_days (M): reversal 83f7710b-69c1-454c-af85-552b8a489775 2025-12-13..14 (recertification due 2025-12-12, signed 2025-12-15) -> 2; baseline 0 -> 1990.25.
All-baseline 3851.75. T2: with every other factor at baseline (s_e 100) each method still moves the figure because s_l is the non-factor tier share (25 here); s_e moves alone because the base split keeps E > 0; the rate moves alone everywhere.
Near-misses: the declined-hold reservation 98d77a7c-4238-416e-9bef-036258c68a86 books no held day (only the Medicare reversal takes the night off); the bed-hold charge row is not a held-day row; the carrier charge is not the resident's.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. medicare_evt_coinsurance.charge_once: the December block has a carrier charge and no resident charge -> a resident charge may be posted once. medicare_evt_day_counting: covered days = booked 29 - reversed 3 = 26 (midnight census; inpatient night and uncertified days not covered). No time gate engaged.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Object: the resident's original charge for b6959ca7-0102-4c57-ac00-b5d846a9201c; rows read: the November block and its resident charge (earlier share), the two December reversals, the December held leave; excluded: the carrier's charges, the November payments, the bed-hold charge rows, the declined reservation.

WORLD ROWS. Customer, coverage (plan L, eff 2025-12-16, last certification 2025-12-15, covered days used 52, balance 3561.50), November days 1-20 and 21-26 blocks with 50/50 charges and their payments, December block (29 booked), hospital-day and uncertified reversals (2026-01-02, before the carrier charge), carrier charge 3561.50 on 26 days (crossover), bed-hold: held hospital leave (notice, election, booked days, 768.00 charge) and the declined hospital-leave reservation (notice, decline election).
KNOWN RESIDUE (T0-F1, C11; least-bad, see worklog): base makes the carrier's share the block total less the resident amount, so the seeded carrier row lets the resident figure be backed out; and the card payment equals the open balance the charge leaves. Kept and stated: not seeding the carrier row leaves a carrier charge owed outside the drawn two-problem tree, and every payment in this charter applies to one charge up to its open balance.

PERSONA. Joan (daughter, representative) asks to pay December by card; gives name, DOB, phone; answers Medigap and absence questions only when asked (December 6-8 held, December 10 overnight inpatient admission with the hold declined); consents to whatever the office must do; completes the card payment the agent hands over; ends.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Draw: prerequisite_problems 1, factor_counts [5, 5]. Root medicare_ext_card_payment_share (user) <- value_input (cnt_days) <- medicare_ext_resident_block_share (agent). State-form sentence above; only the charge tool writes a resident charge. False at opening: no resident charge names b6959ca7-0102-4c57-ac00-b5d846a9201c. Deletion: skip the charge -> the card computation counts no day (0.00) and has no charge to name.

STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers -> verify (DOB + phone) -> coverage -> ledger -> bed-hold reservations, ledger, elections -> post the resident charge 1885.50 (26 days, 209.50) -> hand over the card payment 1885.50 against the new charge.

VERIFICATION. Scratch verify_r2.py (removed at the end) evaluated the published compute with check_compute's sandbox on initial_state and after the charge: 1885.50 / 1885.50; factor figures as listed. Gates for task 0 re-run green (see worklog).


ROUND 3. (1) One scope sentence shared verbatim by all five policies names every sibling's case and, for every block outside the record test, restates the retired base split clause in full (Medigap split from the carrier's policy effective date, QMB from the first day of the month after the determination, earlier split before the date). (2) The record test adds: when the resident's charge stands, its day count equals the booked days less every reversal posted on or before the charge (so 'posted on or before / after the charge' is exact); the correction's test also requires a last service date in 2024 or later. (3) The card payment counts the block's covered days once the resident's charge stands (gate cnt_days), so it agrees with the bank-draft rule and the open balance. (4) The reduction for reversed covered days prices only an uncertified reversal posted after the charge (compute tests the posting date). (5) Nights the resident was away without admission are leave-of-absence days and inpatient nights are hospital days, as base defines them; the hospital-day reversals in these worlds are one-night inpatient admissions. (6) The correction's year-rate ladder falls through to 204.00 (the earliest year its record test admits), so every other factor moves the correction alone.

ROUND 4. (1) Both payment rules now state the base posting limit: a payment figure above the resident charge's open balance (amount less payments and adjustments plus returned payments) shows the charge was billed below what its days call for, and the payment is then not taken under the policy (any payment sent is applied only up to the open balance, the rest returned). On this world the figure equals the open balance, so it is taken; each factor's baseline raises the figure above the open balance, so the sensitivity figures are 0.00 (not taken). T2 holds on a producible world where the charge was billed at 217.00 and 100 percent (both errors base names): there the figure never exceeds the open balance and every factor moves alone. (2) The bank-draft wait now names uncertified-day reversals only - the only reversals the reduction policy prices - and the bank draft's record test excludes a hospital-day or leave-of-absence reversal posted after the charge. (3) The reduction's record test adds a last service date in 2024 or later and an open balance above nothing, so whenever it waits on a rate-year correction that correction can be written.

ROUND 5. (1) Certified funds: superseded in round 6 (see ROUND 6). (2) Every wait is now engaged only where its resolver writes a positive figure: the card waits on the resident charge where the block's covered days take a resident share above nothing; the reduction waits on the rate-year correction where, in addition, the days take such a share; the bank draft waits on reductions only for uncertified-day reversals posted after the charge that take back such days. The bank draft's record test adds a 2024-or-later block and an open balance above nothing (the reduction's own test). All three waits are engaged and unmet at the opening of the task worlds. (3) Half-up rounding is computed as RND(x + 0.000000001, 2) on the summed figure; the tools round with an exact Decimal half-up helper. Scored figures are unchanged. (4) The resident charge's and the card payment's record tests also require a last service date in 2024 or later, so every policy's year-rate ladder prices only years it states (a pre-2024 block is outside every record test).

ROUND 6. The certified-funds override of round 5 is withdrawn: the base sentence 'Once the resident has had the returned-payment limit of dishonored payments within the rolling lookback of calendar months ending on the payment date, only certified funds are accepted from the resident on any coverage episode.' stays in force unchanged. Each payment rule now says that whether the payment may be taken at all is settled by that base sentence (an eligibility condition, judged from the resident's dishonored payments on every episode), and that the policy prices the payment only where one may be taken. Neither task world carries a dishonored payment on any episode, so the payment is accepted; the solvability contract cites that evidence. Scored figures are unchanged.

ROUND 7. (QMB treatment; superseded in round 8, see ROUND 8.)
user_scenario:
You are Joan Calloway, Harold Dunmore's daughter. Your father has been at the Keystone Ridge center in Camp Hill, room 116-B, since early November, getting back on his feet after a hospital stay, and you look after his bills; the business office has you on file as his representative, and the phone number on his account, 717-555-0143, is your cell. You are calling on a weekday morning, a little hurried, polite but to the point, and you keep your sentences short. You open by saying: "I'd like to pay my dad's December Medicare coinsurance by card today." You know from the November statement that the center started billing a coinsurance share once he was past his twentieth day, and you paid November by check, but you have not seen anything for December and you would rather settle it now than have it waiting while you travel later this month. You have no idea how the amount is worked out, you never offer a figure, and paying December is the only thing you want from this call.

When the agent asks who the resident is, you give his full name, Harold Dunmore. When the agent needs to confirm details, you give his date of birth, 1937-08-14 (August 14, 1937), and your phone number, 717-555-0143; only if the agent asks for something more do you add the last four digits of his Social Security number, 1462, or your email, joan.calloway@ptd.net. If the agent asks about his supplemental insurance, you say his Medigap policy is with Commonwealth Mutual Medigap and that the company switched him from Plan K to Plan L partway through December; you remember the new card says the change started December 16. If the agent asks whether he was away from the center at any point, you say he was taken to the hospital by ambulance on the evening of December 6, kept two nights for observation, and came back on December 8, and that you asked the center to hold his room; and that on the evening of December 10 he was admitted to the hospital again overnight and came back the next day, and that time you told the center not to hold the bed. If the agent asks whether it may take care of whatever the business office needs to do on his account so that December can be paid, you say yes, go ahead.

When the agent tells you the December amount, you accept it; you have nothing to compare it with. When the agent hands the card payment over to you, you complete it yourself for exactly the amount and the charge the agent gives you; if the agent asks for your card number instead, you say you would rather enter it yourself through the payment the agent hands you. Once the payment has gone through and the agent confirms it, you thank them and say goodbye.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The latest booked coinsurance block is the December 2025 entry; the only charge naming it is the Medigap carrier's.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: post_coinsurance_charge_97c12690 creates a resident charge naming b6959ca7-0102-4c57-ac00-b5d846a9201c; cnt_days then reads the block's covered days.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge: the resident charge is written first and the card payment second; the payment counts the block's covered days only once that charge stands.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the charge leaves no resident charge on the December block: cnt_days stays 0, the card computation counts no day (0.00 instead of 1885.50) and there is no charge to name.
